lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p20 - Point and say.

details: Point and say activates vocabulary within the new grammar context. Students identify the characters and the jobs in the pictures (firefighter, vet) before listening to the dialogue.
Look for accurate pointing to the specific speech bubbles or thought bubbles and naming the jobs shown.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p20 - Listen to the conversation. Act it out.

details: Listen and act develops narrative comprehension and fluency. Students follow the audio story about the girls' parents and then role-play the Q&A structure "What does your mummy do?"
Look for attentive listening and confident use of the structure "My [mummy/daddy]'s a [job]" during the role-play.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p20 - Read and circle. Then draw.

details: Read, circle and draw consolidates the grammar through reading and personalization. Students read the prompt "What does your daddy/mummy do?", circle the correct parent word (if applicable), and draw the job in the box.
Look for a recognizable drawing of a job (e.g., a stethoscope for a doctor) and circling the correct family word.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p66 - Ask and answer for the girl and boy.

details: Ask and answer checks interpretation of visuals. Students look at the thought bubbles (female doctor, male police officer) and practice the third-person structure "She's a doctor" / "He's a police officer."
Look for correct gender pronouns (She vs He) matching the character in the thought bubble.

details: Ask and answer applies the structure to the student's real life. Students work in pairs to ask about their own parents' professions.
Look for confident production of the sentence "My [mummy/daddy] is a [job]" using the vocabulary learned in the unit.

details: Ask and answer provides controlled practice of the target structure. Students share their drawings with a partner, asking "What does he/she do?" and answering.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p20 - 5. Sing the song and do the actions

details: Sing the song reinforces the grammar pattern through rhythm. Students sing the lyrics asking about family jobs ("What does your daddy do?") and answering ("He's a firefighter") while doing the respective actions.
Look for enthusiastic singing, staying in time with the music, and clear pronunciation of the questions and answers.
